purpose: ngspice's VDMOS gate charge through a -10 V to 5 V gate step: the default gate capacitances (vdmosset.c:70-80), the atan/tanh Cgd law (devsup.c:654-665) integrated to a charge, and the instance m making m parallel copies, twice the gate charge at m=2, as ngspice master does (2bc63e, 6bd5c2) where 44.2 and 45 leave the caps unscaled (vdmosload.c:71-74). ESPice gave this card no gate capacitance, so v(g1) followed the source and both currents were 0.

oracle.derivation: ngspice 44.2 batch run of this deck with M2 (m=2) written as two m=1 instances on the same nodes, which is what m means in ngspice master (2bc63e "VDMOS scaling fixed", 6bd5c2) and what 44.2 computes correctly; every 10th of its 2520 accepted time points (and the last) read from its ASCII raw, and ngspice 45 gives the same bytes on that netlist. Corroborated by an independent model: m C_tot(v) dv/dt = (vp(t) - v)/10 with C_tot = CGS + Cgd(v), integrated by RK4 at 2 ps, i(vd) = m Cgd(v) dv/dt, i(vs) = m CGS dv/dt. ngspice sits within 9e-5 of each column's peak of it at m=1 (peaks 10 V, 0.746 A, 0.994 A) and within 7e-5 at m=2 (10 V, 0.726 A, 1.177 A).
oracle.command: sed -E 's/^([^ *.]+)(.*) m=2$/\1_1\2\n\1_2\2/' vdmos_gate_charge.sp > vdmos_gate_charge_x.sp && SPICE_ASCIIRAWFILE=1 ngspice -n -b -r ref.raw vdmos_gate_charge_x.sp
oracle.tolerance: rtol 1e-3 with atol 1e-3 V and 2e-4 A. The deck sets RELTOL 1e-4: at ngspice's default 1e-3 its currents sit up to 7e-4 of their peak off the exact charge ODE, which no 1e-3 comparison can carry. ngspice accumulates q += (C_n + C_(n-1))/2 dv (vdmosload.c:508-513), ESPice integrates the closed-form charge; at a 0.1 ns step the two agree well inside these bounds.
